title: Variational Quantum Simulation of the Interacting Schwinger Model on a Trapped-Ion Quantum Processor
abstract: Explores the multi-flavor lattice Schwinger model — a toy model for QCD — in 1+1 dimensions with nonzero chemical potential via variational quantum simulation on a shuttling-based trapped-ion quantum processor. Fermionic problem intractable classically due to sign problem. Employs parametric quantum circuit to identify ground states in different parameter regimes, mapping out a quantum phase transition. Output states analyzed via quantum state tomography to reveal how correlations change across the phase transition.
key_claims: Multi-flavor Schwinger model with nonzero chemical potential simulated on trapped-ion hardware
Sign problem evaded by variational approach on quantum hardware
Quantum phase transition mapped out and analyzed via state tomography
Demonstrates trapped-ion processor utility for 1+1D QFT beyond classical reach
supports_or_contradicts: NEUTRAL — demonstrates QFT-on-hardware capability for 1+1D model (same dimensionality as our Ising CFT). No direct bearing on holographic force result; contextually relevant as sign-problem-evading hardware QFT.
